lines.trans: So, cooks, place bets and sign up!
Now Fedya and Max will prepare a dish each.
And the chef will taste and choose the winner.
What is the main ingredient for our dish?
The main ingredient of today's contest is cod!
You are finished, runt!
I have cooked all the fish in the ocean!
I also know how to cook fish.
We will see your pathetic skills.
Who bets five hundred rubles on Fedya?
All the cooks in the kitchen bet on me.
And I will prove my talent anyway!
Time has started, begin cooking right now!
I will make the best sauce.

And the chef will taste and choose the winner.
What is the main ingredient for our dish?
The main ingredient of today's contest is cod!

And the chef will taste and choose the winner.

The main ingredient of today's contest is cod!

All the cooks in the kitchen bet on me.

Time has started, begin cooking right now!
I will make the best sauce.
See you!

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'dish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: Serve the hot dishes.
This is the restaurant's signature dish.

examples.text: Настоящий повар чувствует каждый вкус блюда.
examples.trans: A real chef feels every taste of the dish.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: How is it in Hungary?
I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
As you all know...
Share with everyone.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'time', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I don't have time.
We're having a good time.

examples.text: Я и сама хорошо проведу время.
examples.trans: I'll have a good time on my own.

meanings.note: after a plural noun or pronoun: вы все
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (всем = to everyone (dative)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You're all thieves.
Nobody cares.

examples.text: И знаешь, что самое главное? Всем всё равно.
examples.trans: And you know the main thing? Nobody cares.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'meeting', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('see you') (in 'до встречи' = until we meet) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: See you!
I have a meeting.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
Secondary conversational sense ('that's it, done') (at the start of a sentence) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Everything's fine.
That's it, bye!

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.en: to choose, select; to use up completely (quotas, limits)
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to choose', forming an aspectual pair with 'выбирать'.

examples.text: В этом году все квоты выбрали.
examples.trans: This year all the quotas have been used up.
She chose the most beautiful dress.
Agreed, I will choose a movie.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'main' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
Secondary conversational sense ('the main thing') (neuter главное, used as a noun) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
This is the main street.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cook; to prepare', paired with 'приготовить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to prepare') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm cooking lunch.
Mum cooks well.

examples.text: Я уже не могу готовить, стирать, убирать. Я хочу на море!
examples.trans: I can't take the cooking, washing and cleaning any more. I want to go to the sea!

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to do, to make', paired with 'сделать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to make') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: What are you doing?
I'm making dinner.
Hi, Arkady Borisovich. What are you doing?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'until' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('goodbye') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Goodbye!
See you tomorrow!
See you tonight!

meanings.note: что и требовалось доказать = Q.E.D., which is what needed to be proved

examples.trans: There, which is what needed to be proved!
He could not prove anything.

examples.text: Я обязательно докажу своё кулинарное мастерство.
examples.trans: I will definitely prove my culinary mastery.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('pathetic, pitiful').

examples.trans: Those were pathetic attempts.
We will see your pathetic skills.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'писываться'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to be recorded', forming an aspectual pair with 'записаться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Everything is recorded on camera.
Of course, everything is recorded on camera.

examples.text: Итак, повара, делаем ставки и записываемся!
examples.trans: So, cooks, place bets and sign up!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'so', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: So, look carefully.
So, look here, Samsonov.

examples.text: Итак, у нас конкурс детских поделок.
examples.trans: And so, we have a children's craft contest.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('what') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.trans: What is your town like?
What a beautiful house!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
Secondary conversational sense ('' ' = over and out') (radio and phone phrase) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is the end.
Over and out.
At the end of the film everyone is happy.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'contest', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: We have a children's craft contest.
She won in the musical competition.
Craft contest at the daycare.

meanings.note: in the instrumental: 'кем ты работаешь?'

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Who's there?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Entered Russian via Polish 'kuchnia' and Middle High German 'küchen', ultimately from Late Latin 'coquina' (from 'coquere', to cook).
Secondary conversational sense ('cuisine, cooking') (русская кухня = Russian cuisine) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: We're sitting in the kitchen.
Three rooms and a big kitchen.
And the kitchen is over there.

meanings.note: лучший в мире = the best in the world
Secondary conversational sense ('better') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: This is the best day!
You're my best friend.

examples.text: Ты мне даёшь пятьсот рублей, а я выхожу и покупаю тебе лучшую приставку в мире.
examples.trans: You give me five hundred roubles, and I get out and buy you the best console in the world.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'чинать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to begin, to start', paired with 'начать'.

examples.trans: When do I start?
The lesson starts at nine.

examples.text: Аркаш, ну что скажешь? Когда начинать?
examples.trans: Arkasha, so what do you say? When do I start?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.trans: I love our town.
This is our flat.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: playful derogatory nickname used by Chef Barinov for Max

examples.trans: Runt, are you still standing here?
The chef often called the newcomer a runt.

examples.text: Огузок, ты официально принят в штат нашего ресторана!
examples.trans: Rump, you are officially hired onto our restaurant staff!

meanings.note: Северный Ледовитый океан = the Arctic Ocean

examples.trans: The plane is flying over the ocean.
I want to go to the ocean.

examples.text: Я уже всё решил. Одну треть на кладбище, две трети над океаном.
examples.trans: I've already sorted it all out. One third goes to the cemetery, two thirds over the ocean.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'along' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('along, around') (+ dative) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('by (phone)') ('по телефону') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm here about the job.
We're talking on the phone.

examples.text: Это Аракелян. Я по поводу торгового центра.
examples.trans: It's Arakelyan. I'm calling about the shopping centre.

meanings.note: Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'winner', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.trans: Applause for our winner!
The winner received a gold medal.
The name of the grand winner.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'cook', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: There is this English chef.

examples.text: Есть такой английский повар. Я по его передачам научусь готовить.
examples.trans: There is this English chef. I will learn to cook from his shows.

examples.text: Я хочу работать поваром в ресторане.
examples.trans: I want to work as a cook in a restaurant.

meanings.note: Russian perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to go', forming an aspectual pair with 'идти'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: May I go?
Let's go home.
Can I go and have a look?

meanings.en: to try, to taste (food or drink)
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'пробовать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to try', forming an aspectual pair with 'пробовать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to try, to attempt') (+ infinitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Try the tea with bread rings.
I'll try one more time.
Let's try.

meanings.en: to have a look, to take a look
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'смотреть'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to have a look', forming an aspectual pair with 'смотреть'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to watch (a film) through') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: May I have a look?
I only had a look.
Can I go and have a look?

приготовить.gloss: to prepare, to cook, to make

meanings.en: to cook, to make (food), to prepare
meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'готовить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to prepare', forming an aspectual pair with 'готовить'.

examples.trans: I made a cake.
Mum cooked a delicious dinner.

examples.text: Я торт приготовила. Ты любишь сладкое?
examples.trans: I made a cake. Do you have a sweet tooth?

meanings.note: Prefix 'про-' indicates movement through, completion, or missing the mark (stem 'дукт'). Common masculine noun meaning 'product, foodstuff' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Fresh food products.

examples.text: Ты будешь целый день разгружать продукты!
examples.trans: You will unload groceries the whole day!
The guests need the freshest product!

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'straight'.
Secondary conversational sense ('straight ahead') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Just like that?
Go straight along this street.

examples.text: В смысле, Виктор Степанович? Прямо так, да?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Viktor Stepanovich? Just like that?

meanings.note: Russian numeral ('five hundred') that declines for case and governs case agreement on the counted noun.

examples.trans: It costs five hundred roubles.
About five hundred roubles.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: almost always in 'всё равно' = it doesn't matter; мне всё равно = I don't care

examples.trans: I don't care.
Nobody cares.

examples.text: Мне всё равно. Что ты, что он.
examples.trans: It's all the same to me. You or him.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'rouble', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: This costs a hundred roubles.
I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.
examples.trans: Our task is to take a billion roubles from the bribe-takers.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'fish', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: A big platter of fish and crabs.

examples.text: На ужин мы приготовили свежую рыбу.
examples.trans: For dinner we cooked fresh fish.

examples.text: У нас есть большая тарелка рыбы и крабов.
examples.trans: We have a big platter of fish and crabs.

meanings.note: forms the superlative: самый главный = the most important
Secondary conversational sense ('the very') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The most important thing is the people.
It's the biggest town.
Do you know the main thing?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.trans: He keeps his word.
They are building their houses.

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.trans: We've done a lot.
I'll do it tomorrow.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодняшний'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('today's').

examples.trans: What is today's menu?
The main ingredient of today's contest is cod!

examples.text: С сегодняшнего дня говорите мне только правду.
examples.trans: From today on, tell me only the truth.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm in the office now.
I'll be right there.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: culinary condiment or liquid topping

examples.text: Паста под соусом была очень вкусной.
examples.trans: The pasta with sauce was very tasty.
The chef prepared a spicy tomato sauce.

examples.text: Сегодня на ужин паста под соусом!
examples.trans: Tonight for dinner we have pasta with sauce!

meanings.en: to put, to place in an upright position
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тавить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'поставить'.

examples.trans: Where should I put the plate?
Put the kettle on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'bet'.
Secondary conversational sense ('rate') (wage or interest rate) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Там наливают бесплатно, если сделать ставку.
examples.trans: They pour for free if you place a bet.
Place your bets, gentlemen players.
The bets are placed, no more bets.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'talent', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: You have no talent.

examples.text: У этой девочки большой талант к музыке.
examples.trans: This girl has a great talent for music.

examples.text: Потому что твой папа прав! У тебя нет таланта.
examples.trans: Because your dad is right! You have no talent.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.trans: This is your coffee.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.
Your boss is here.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'too'.

examples.trans: Me too.
He's here too.

examples.text: Мы же здесь выросли. И о людях тоже надо думать.
examples.trans: After all, we grew up here. And you have to think about people too.

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'cod'.

examples.trans: The main product is cod.
Fresh cod is very tasty.

examples.text: Кто-то вчера разморозил пять килограммов трески.
examples.trans: Someone thawed five kilograms of cod yesterday.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'skill' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.trans: The main thing is the ability to work with people.
That is a useful skill.

examples.text: Главное в нашем деле — умение работать с документами.
examples.trans: The main thing in our work is knowing how to work with documents.

уметь.gloss: to know how to, to be able to

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'меть'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know how to', forming an aspectual pair with 'суметь'.

examples.trans: I can swim.
He can't count.

examples.text: Эх, Паша, Паша. Ты считать не умеешь.
examples.trans: Oh, Pasha, Pasha. You can't count.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
